sheet-1-1.description: The larger map part of the index sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch in the lower right quarter of the page below the key map and street index. It shows Lewis Street running down the left side of the part, south of the stretch on sheet 7, with house numbers 201 to 229 along its west frontage, and High Street leaving it to the east near the foot of the part, with lots numbered 15 to 32 along High. The blocks east of Lewis are deep, narrow residential lots with frame dwellings and small outbuildings, much of the ground behind them open; the rear of the lots is marked 'No exposure' along the east edge. A building on High Street near the bottom is labelled as formerly the public school, to be a dwelling. The strip west of Lewis, behind the heavy line that separates this part from the Wormatia Leather Co. part, carries only the lot numbers of the west side and the reference numbers of sheets 6 and 7, which draw the ground to the north. The foot of the part is lettered 'Vacant beyond'. The part continues sheet 7's Lewis Street lots southward; its top lot line repeats the lowest lot line drawn on sheet 7. North is towards the upper left, as on the other sheets of the atlas. Buildings are almost all frame (yellow), with a few small sheds and a stable.
notes: Placed on the junction of Lewis and High streets and two lot-line corners carried from sheet 7.

Index sheet with key map, street and specials index and town data (top, masked out) and two map parts at 50 ft: part 1 (lower right) Lewis Street south of sheet 7 with High Street; part 2 (lower left, drawn at another angle) Wormatia Leather Co. on the brook by Lewis Street, with the C.R.R. of N.J. passenger station.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: lower left: Wormatia Leather Co. on the brook by Lewis Street, with the C.R.R. of N.J. passenger station (no street junction drawn (Lewis Street ends at an iron bridge, roads beyond are dashed); brook not in the reference data; needs hand-picked control (step 6b): Lewis Street bridge and the railroad, or parcel corners).

sheet-2-1.description: The left of two strips on sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and separated from the right strip by a heavy diagonal line. It shows Broadway (today Broad Street) running from the lower left to the upper right, north-east of sheet 3, crossed near the middle by Monmouth Road (today College Avenue on the north side and Cliffwood Avenue on the south side of Broad Street). Lot numbers run from about 501 to 541 along Broadway, with 15 to 39 along Monmouth Road. The public school, a brick building, stands on Monmouth Road west of Broadway; the D. Rosenberg & Co. underwear factory, in a building owned by E. P. Hendrickson, stands east of Broadway in the lower part of the strip, with its engine house and poultry house. A brook crosses the top of the strip and touches its lower edge. The rest of the strip is scattered frame dwellings, stables, coops and corn cribs on large lots, with much open ground. A 12 inch water pipe runs along Broadway. North on this sheet points to the left of the page. The strip carries the reference numbers of sheets 2 and 3 at its ends; its upper end continues in the right strip of the same sheet.
notes: Broadway is today Broad Street; Monmouth Road at Broadway is today College Avenue (north) and Cliffwood Avenue (south).
Placed on one hand-picked junction with the scale and north direction set in the config; low confidence.

Broadway (Broad Street) north-east of sheet 3 in two strips divided by a heavy line: part 1 (left) Broadway at Monmouth Road (now College Avenue / Cliffwood Avenue), public school, Rosenberg underwear factory; part 2 (right) Broadway further east at a 'Street not named' and the brook.

sheet-2-2.description: The right of two strips on sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch to the right of the heavy diagonal line that divides the sheet. It continues Broadway (today Broad Street) further east from the upper end of the left strip, with lot numbers about 519 to 539 on one side and 560 to 577 on the other. A street lettered 'Street' and noted as not named leaves Broadway to the south in the lower half of the strip; today this is probably Brook Street. A brook crosses the upper part of the strip and passes under Broadway. The ground is mostly large residential lots with frame dwellings, stables, coops, corn cribs and a storage shed along the unnamed street; a 12 inch water pipe runs along Broadway. North points to the left of the page. The left edge of the strip, along the dividing line, is lettered 'Vacant beyond'.
notes: The cross street is printed as 'Street' with the note 'not named'; identified with today's Brook Street at Broad Street from the distance along Broadway; low confidence.
Placed on one detected junction with the scale set in the config and rotation from its measured lines.

Broadway (Broad Street) north-east of sheet 3 in two strips divided by a heavy line: part 1 (left) Broadway at Monmouth Road (now College Avenue / Cliffwood Avenue), public school, Rosenberg underwear factory; part 2 (right) Broadway further east at a 'Street not named' and the brook.

sheet-3.description: A sheet at 50 feet to an inch covering the blocks between Railroad Avenue and Broadway north-east of White Street, the residential continuation of the business centre on sheet 5. Railroad Avenue runs along the left edge with the track of the Central Railroad of New Jersey in it; Broadway (today Broad Street) runs up the middle and bends to the north-east near the top, where it continues on sheet 2. White Street crosses the foot of the sheet. Morris Place (today Kellys Lane) joins Railroad Avenue and Broadway in the upper half, and Burns (today Byrnes Lane) leaves Broadway to the east just beyond it. The blocks hold frame dwellings with stables and sheds; institutions include the Baptist Church and the Presbyterian Church on the east side of Broadway and the Episcopal Church, a stone building, west of it; a blacksmith shop stands behind the Broadway frontage. The east side of the sheet is mostly deep lots with open ground behind. Water pipes run in Broadway. North on the sheet points to the upper left. Lot numbers on Railroad Avenue run about 236 to 273 and on Broadway 337 to 372.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today Throckmorton Avenue; Broadway is Broad Street; Morris Place is Kellys Lane; Burns is Byrnes Lane.
Railroad Avenue is drawn with the rails inside it; the detector setting double_line_ft 5 keeps the rails from being taken for a street edge.
Railroad Av (Throckmorton Avenue, C.R.R. of N.J. along it), Broadway (Broad Street), White, Morris Pl. (Kellys Lane), Burns (Byrnes Lane). Churches. Rails in Railroad Av.

sheet-4.description: A sheet at 50 feet to an inch covering the west side of Railroad Avenue and the open ground beyond it, north of Main Street. The track of the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs down the right edge in Railroad Avenue, with a row of dwellings on deep lots, numbered about 201 to 222, facing it; the Methodist Episcopal church stands among them. White Street meets Railroad Avenue from the east at the right edge. Further west the G. W. Loverside underwear factory stands on the open block. A creek runs the length of the sheet and passes under Main Street at the bottom; west of it is a farm with barn, hay shed, storage, wagon shed, windmill, corn cribs, an ice house and an auto shed, and a dwelling near Main. Main Street crosses the foot of the sheet with lots numbered 85 to 106 and a 10 inch water pipe. The greater part of the sheet is open ground. North points to the upper left.
notes: Railroad Avenue (not lettered here) is today Throckmorton Avenue.
Placed on two hand-picked junctions along Railroad Avenue (helmert); the detected Main Street junction paired a rail with a street edge and was excluded.
West side of Railroad Av (Throckmorton Avenue) and C.R.R. of N.J. north of Main; creek, farm buildings, Loverside underwear factory. Only Main and Railroad Av junctions.

sheet-5.description: The business centre of Eatontown at 50 feet to an inch: Main Street down the left side, Railroad Avenue across the top with its railroad track, Broadway (today Broad Street) across the middle, and White Street on the right. Lewis Street meets Main from the west between Railroad Avenue and Broadway, and below Broadway Main continues as South Street, curving to the south-west. The block between Railroad Avenue and Broadway holds the commercial frontage on Main (candy and tobacco, seed and produce, cobbler, grocery, drugs, hardware, meat) and the brick Metropolitan Hotel with its stables, then bakery, barber and harness shops, a printing office and dwellings along Broadway, and St. Dorothea's Roman Catholic church. South of Broadway are the post office and public library, an auto garage, the Masonic Hall, the Second Advent church on South Street, and the large MacFarland Park Horse Market with its carriage house, hen coops, store house and poultry house. Water pipes of 6 to 12 inches run in the streets. North points to the upper right on this sheet.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today Throckmorton Avenue; Broadway is Broad Street.
Pilot sheet of the atlas.
Pilot. Main, Railroad Av (Throckmorton Avenue), Broadway (Broad Street), White, Lewis, South. Business centre, Metropolitan Hotel, St. Dorothea R.C. church, MacFarland Park horse market.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of sheet 6, at 50 feet to an inch, covering Main Street west of Railroad Avenue and the ground south of it. Main Street crosses the top of the sheet; Tinton Falls Avenue leaves it to the south-west at the upper left. The Mill Pond fills the middle of the sheet, fed from the creek of sheet 4 and drained under Main by the C. B. Richmond flour mill. East of the pond are a lumber yard with lumber sheds, piles, a painting shop and ice houses, and coal sheds along the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which runs down Railroad Avenue. Further east, on Lewis Street, are the town hall and fire department with its hook and ladder truck and chemical engine, a flour, feed and hay store, Crescent Hall, and a row of dwellings on lots 7 to 21. On Tinton Falls Avenue are dwellings on large lots. The lower left of the sheet, inside a heavy outline, is a separate inset (part 2) and is not covered here. North points to the upper left.
notes: Tinton Falls Avenue is today Tinton Avenue; Railroad Avenue north of Main is today Throckmorton Avenue, the stretch south of Main no longer exists as a street.
Placed on three hand-picked junctions along Main Street (helmert); low confidence away from Main.

Main west of Railroad Av: part 1 Main with Tinton Falls Av (Tinton Avenue), Mill Pond, flour mill, lumber yard, Railroad Av south of Main, Lewis, town hall; part 2 (inset in heavy outline, lower left) Tinton Falls Av lots 101-116 further south-west.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset in heavy outline: Tinton Falls Av lots 101-116 (no street junction; position along Tinton Avenue unknown; needs hand-picked control (step 6b): parcel corners once the lot run is identified).

sheet-7.description: A sheet at 50 feet to an inch covering the ground south of Main Street between Lewis Street and South Street. Main Street runs across the top with the stub of Broadway coming in from above; Lewis Street runs down the left edge with lots numbered 22 to 41; South Street leaves Main at the top and runs diagonally to the lower right, with dwellings on lots 5 to 20; Crow leaves South Street near the right edge. The Main Street frontage holds a row of shops: barber, restaurant, furniture and undertaker, bicycle, dry goods, cobbler and general store, with a blacksmith shop and carriage repair and painting shops behind on Lewis. A large wedge-shaped tract in the middle of the sheet is open ground with a hot house; the rest is frame dwellings with coops, sheds and storage buildings. North points to the upper left.
notes: Crow is probably today's Willow Street; Broadway is Broad Street.
Main Street from Broadway to South Street follows today's Main Street (NJ 35) only for its first block: South Street is today's South Street.
Main, South St., Crow, Lewis (lots 22-41), Broadway at top edge. 1909 South St. is the modern Main Street (NJ 35) towards Kremer Avenue; to be confirmed from the fit.
